html:
A Palawa woman of the Nuenonne people of Bruny Island, Tasmania, who lived through the destruction of Aboriginal Tasmanian society under British colonisation. She was long, and wrongly, called the last Aboriginal Tasmanian.

In her youth, during the Black War between settlers and Aboriginal people, she lost her mother, her sister and the man she was to marry to violence by sealers, whalers and others. In 1830 she joined George Augustus Robinson on his "Friendly Mission", which persuaded the remaining Aboriginal people to leave their lands. Most were moved to Wybalenna on Flinders Island, where many died of disease and despair.

She went with Robinson to Port Phillip, where she joined a small band that attacked settlers; two of the men were hanged in 1842. She ended her life at Oyster Cove near Hobart. After her death her skeleton was dug up and put on show in a Hobart museum until 1947. In 1976, a century after she died, her remains were cremated and scattered in the channel near her birthplace, as she had asked. Other Palawa survived, and their descendants live in Tasmania today, as do the older traditions she carried.
